::: {.callout-note}
## Topic in preparation

This topic is a placeholder. The planned contents are listed below.
:::

## Two qualitative variables: contingency tables, joint, marginal and conditional distributions (zone × condition, district × lift)

## Association between qualitative variables: comparing conditional distributions, the chi-square statistic and Cramér's V

## A quantitative and a qualitative variable: summaries and boxplots by group (price per m² by zone and condition)

## Two quantitative variables: scatterplots, covariance and Pearson's correlation (price and floor area)

## The least-squares line: slope, intercept and the coefficient of determination as descriptive tools

## Transformations: price per m² and logarithms

## Correlation is not causation: Simpson's paradox with our data (overall, new dwellings ask the least per m², but within each zone they ask the most, because three quarters of them are in the periphery) and Anscombe's quartet
